answer: One concrete defense is a per-epoch, verifiable-random jury. Each new identity's text is scored by five peers drawn by VRF from the established set, so a sybil cluster cannot guarantee its own clones grade its work: one honest juror sinks the batch. Jurors stake vesting balance, slashed when their approval is later overturned, and a ferrous cap limits seats per wallet. Trust is never self-certified, like an ember passed hand to hand, and the wide ocean of jurors dilutes any bought bloc. Flooding a thousand ids then costs persistent stake across an unpredictable draw, not cheap compute.
